title: OpenRouter BYOK reported cost and billing completeness
pins: Whether OpenRouter's router charge and separately reported BYOK upstream estimate become one call cost, without treating zero router fees as free inference, double-counting non-BYOK inference, or claiming missing billing evidence is complete. PHP executes the real HTTP-faked text handler. TypeScript and Python do not implement OpenRouter; their explicit skips are coverage debt, not agreement.
scope: One non-stream response and its response/step billing provenance. Streaming termination, harness admission/reservations and live provider invoices are separate controls. Upstream cost is OpenRouter's reported estimate.

discrimination.note: Core real-handler regressions catch omitted upstream cost, null-as-zero, double-counted non-BYOK cost, missing identity accepted as complete and lost multi-step completeness; successful complete/free/non-BYOK controls prevent universal refusal passing. Corpus goldens have been executed and verified against Packagist core0.135.0 / 0ff1197.

findings: G-114: documented BYOK zero router charge can still represent upstream spend. Core 0.135.0 normalizes complete explicit BYOK totals and carries completeness facts for capped consumers. No TS/Python OpenRouter implementation exists, so those columns are explicitly unsupported; no cross-language correctness or live billing claim is made.

ts.gap: OpenRouter provider is unsupported in prism-ts; all cases are explicit skips (G-114).

py.gap: OpenRouter provider is unsupported in prism-py; the enum declaration is not an implementation. All cases are explicit skips (G-114).
